 Job Scan Home / GST / Indian Subsidiary and Foreign Parent Are Separate Legal Entities for Export-of-Services Assessment: GSTAT GST Law Report Indian Subsidiary and Foreign Parent Are Separate Legal Entities for Export-of-Services Assessment: GSTAT
 Pro Assessee · More rulings on ITC → · Refund → 
 Separate incorporation and principal-to-principal agreements supported export treatment, leading to refund of unutilised ITC with statutory interest.
 By  Kavi Priya · 2 Nov 2026, 5:50 pm IST 2′ read Save Get the day's tax rulings in your inbox 
 Email address Subscribe × The New Delhi Principal Bench of the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) held that an Indian subsidiary and its foreign parent company are separate legal entities while determining whether services qualify as exports under the IGST Act. 
 Expedia Online Travel Services India Private Limited (the appellant), an indirectly wholly owned subsidiary of Expedia Inc., USA, provided software development and business support services to its overseas group companies under separate agreements.
 Headnote The case number, coram and counsel for this order are part of the subscriber record. 
 Citation 2026 TAXSCAN (GSTAT) 290 Court Goods & Services Tax Appellate Tribunal Subscribe below to read the full record.
